references.text: Here God gives instructions to Aaron about burning fragrant incense on the incense altar every morning and evening, which is the original command that Moses now carries out in Exodus 40:27.
Describes the recipe for the fragrant incense (קְטֹרֶת סַמִּים) to be used on the incense altar, the same expression used in Exodus 40:27.
The making of the incense altar by Bezalel, along with the holy anointing oil and the incense, which are now put into use by Moses.
Aaron is to take incense and burn it before the Lord on the Day of Atonement, showing the continued use of the incense altar in tabernacle service.
Only Aaron's descendants shall burn incense before the Lord's presence, confirming the holy service at the incense altar.
Zechariah serves at the incense altar in the temple and burns incense, a direct continuation of the practice Moses inaugurated in Exodus 40:27.
An angel stands by the altar with incense rising together with the prayers of the saints, an image built upon the incense offerings in the tabernacle.
Verse 16 summarizes Moses' total obedience, which verse 27 specifies through the offering of incense.
Both verses are concrete parts of the same consecration act in Exodus 40.
Connects the consecration of the tabernacle (incense) with the consecration of the priests (offering), both as examples of obedience.
Contrasting cultic actions (inside/outside) that both emphasize total obedience to God's command.
Preparation (making of incense) and fulfillment (use of incense) in the account of consecration.
